# Data Import

```{r}
# Import the dataset
data <- read.csv("health_dataset.csv")

# Remove extra spaces from column names
names(data) <- trimws(names(data))

# View the first few rows
head(data)

# Check the variable names
names(data)

# View the table structure
str(data)
```

# Data Cleaning

```{r}
# Clean your selected variables
cleaned_data <- subset(as.data.frame(data),
              select = c(
                Life_satisfaction,
                Age,
                Gen_health_state,
                Work_hours,
                High_BP,
                Stress_level,
                Sense_belonging,
                Total_income,
                Gender,
                Marital_status))

head(cleaned_data)
str(cleaned_data)

```

# Data Description

```{r}
# 1. Convert special missing-value codes to NA
lapply(cleaned_data, table, useNA = "ifany")

# convert invalid or special missing-value codes to NA before generating missing-value summary
# Record the original number of observations
original_n <- nrow(cleaned_data)

# Life satisfaction: 97 = Don't know, 98 = Refusal, 99 = Not stated
cleaned_data$Life_satisfaction[
  cleaned_data$Life_satisfaction %in% c(97, 98, 99)
] <- NA

# Age: Codes 1-5 are valid categories
# No special missing codes specified in the provided codebook

# General health: 6, 7 = Don't know, 8, 9 = Refusal
cleaned_data$Gen_health_state[
  cleaned_data$Gen_health_state %in% c(6, 7, 8, 9)
] <- NA

# Work hours: special codes
cleaned_data$Work_hours[
  cleaned_data$Work_hours %in% c(96, 99)
] <- NA

# High blood pressure: 7 = Don't know, 8 = Refusal
cleaned_data$High_BP[
  cleaned_data$High_BP %in% c(7, 8)
] <- NA

# Stress level: 7 = Don't know, 8 = Refusal
cleaned_data$Stress_level[
  cleaned_data$Stress_level %in% c(7, 8)
] <- NA

# Sense of belonging: 7 = Don't know,
# 8 = Refusal, 9 = Not stated
cleaned_data$Sense_belonging[
  cleaned_data$Sense_belonging %in% c(7, 8, 9)
] <- NA

# Total income: 9 = Not stated
cleaned_data$Total_income[
  cleaned_data$Total_income == 9
] <- NA

# Gender: 9 = Not stated
cleaned_data$Gender[
  cleaned_data$Gender == 9
] <- NA

# Marital status: 3, 6 = Valid skip, 9 = Not stated
cleaned_data$Marital_status[
  cleaned_data$Marital_status %in% c(3, 6, 9)
] <- NA

```
```{r}
# Missing value summary

missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(cleaned_data),
  Missing = sapply(cleaned_data, function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  Missing_Percent = round(
    sapply(cleaned_data, function(x) mean(is.na(x)) * 100),
    2
  )
)

missing_summary
```

```{r}
# Remove observations with missing values in any variable

complete_data <- na.omit(cleaned_data)

# exported the cleaned dataset
write.csv(
  complete_data,
  "cleaned_health_dataset.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Count observations before and after removing missing values

original_n <- nrow(cleaned_data)
remaining_n <- nrow(complete_data)
removed_n <- original_n - remaining_n

# Display the results

cat("Original observations:", original_n, "\n")
cat("Remaining observations:", remaining_n, "\n")
cat("Removed observations:", removed_n, "\n")
cat("Number of predictors:", ncol(complete_data) - 1, "\n")

cat("Percentage of observations retained:",
    round(remaining_n / original_n * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

```{r}
#3. Check outlier of continuous variables using IQR
model_data <- complete_data
check_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR_value <- IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)

  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_value
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_value

  outliers <- x[x < lower | x > upper]

  cat("Lower bound:", lower, "\n")
  cat("Upper bound:", upper, "\n")
  cat("Number of potential outliers:", length(outliers), "\n")
}

print("IQR summary for life_satisfaction:")
check_outliers(model_data$Life_satisfaction)

print("IQR summary for work_hours:")
check_outliers(model_data$Work_hours)
```

```{r gender-workhours-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center', fig.cap='Life satisfaction and weekly work hours by gender among complete-case respondents. Lines represent descriptive linear trends.'}

#4. Evidence for interaction between Gender and Work_Hours by fitting regression line for each gender

# Create a plotting dataset without modifying model_data
plot_data <- data.frame(
  Work_hours = model_data$Work_hours,
  Life_satisfaction = model_data$Life_satisfaction,
  Gender = factor(
    model_data$Gender,
    levels = c("1", "2"),
    labels = c("Male", "Female")
  )
)

ggplot(plot_data,
       aes(x = Work_hours,
           y = Life_satisfaction,
           color = Gender)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.025, width = 0.25, height = 0.08) +
geom_smooth(
  method = "lm",
  formula = y ~ x,
  se = TRUE,
  linewidth = 1.3
) +
  labs(
    title = "Work Hours and Life Satisfaction by Gender",
    x = "Weekly work hours",
    y = "Life satisfaction (0–10)",
    color = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

# Preliminary Results

```{r}
# 1. Regression model
# Convert categorical predictors into factors
model_data$Age <- factor(model_data$Age)
model_data$Gen_health_state <- factor(model_data$Gen_health_state)
model_data$High_BP <- factor(model_data$High_BP)
model_data$Stress_level <- factor(model_data$Stress_level)
model_data$Sense_belonging <- factor(model_data$Sense_belonging)
model_data$Total_income <- factor(model_data$Total_income)
model_data$Gender <- factor(model_data$Gender)
model_data$Marital_status <- factor(model_data$Marital_status)

# Fit multiple linear regression with interaction
model <- lm(
  Life_satisfaction ~ Gender * Work_hours +
    Age +
    Gen_health_state +
    High_BP +
    Stress_level +
    Sense_belonging +
    Total_income +
    Marital_status,
  data = model_data
)

# Display regression results
summary(model)
```


```{r selected-coefficients, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# 2. Generate a summary table of selected OLS regression coefficients with estimates, standard errors, 95% confidence intervals, and p-values.
# Selected coefficients
selected_terms <- c(
  "Work_hours",
  "Gender2:Work_hours",
  "Gen_health_state5",
  "Stress_level5",
  "Sense_belonging4",
  "Total_income5"
)

predictor_labels <- c(
  "Work hours (male reference)",
  "Gender x Work hours (female vs male)",
  "Poor vs excellent general health",
  "Extreme vs no stress",
  "Very weak vs very strong belonging",
  "Highest vs lowest income"
)

# Extract coefficients and confidence intervals
coef_info <- summary(model)$coefficients
ci_info <- confint(model)

# Check coefficient names
missing_terms <- setdiff(selected_terms, rownames(coef_info))

if (length(missing_terms) > 0) {
  stop(
    "These coefficients were not found in model: ",
    paste(missing_terms, collapse = ", "),
    "\nAvailable coefficients: ",
    paste(rownames(coef_info), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Build table
selected_table <- data.frame(
  Predictor = predictor_labels,
  Estimate = sprintf("%.4f", coef_info[selected_terms, "Estimate"]),
  SE = sprintf("%.4f", coef_info[selected_terms, "Std. Error"]),
  CI = sprintf(
    "[%.4f, %.4f]",
    ci_info[selected_terms, 1],
    ci_info[selected_terms, 2]
  ),
  p_value = ifelse(
    coef_info[selected_terms, "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001,
    "<0.001",
    sprintf("%.3f", coef_info[selected_terms, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  ),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Automatically match the output format
output_format <- if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  "latex"
} else {
  "pipe"
}

knitr::kable(
  selected_table,
  format = output_format,
  booktabs = (output_format == "latex"),
  escape = TRUE,
  col.names = c("Predictor", "Estimate", "SE", "95% CI", "p-value"),
  caption = paste0(
    "Selected OLS coefficient estimates for life satisfaction ",
    "(n = ", nobs(model), ")."
  )
)
```

```{r}
# 3. Preliminary multiple linear regression results for life satisfaction
# Extract regression coefficient estimates
coef_table <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients)

# Add variable names as a column
coef_table$Variable <- rownames(coef_table)

# Calculate 95% confidence intervals
ci <- confint(model, level = 0.95)

coef_table$CI_Lower <- ci[, 1]
coef_table$CI_Upper <- ci[, 2]

# Select and reorder columns
coef_table <- coef_table[, c(
  "Variable",
  "Estimate",
  "Std. Error",
  "CI_Lower",
  "CI_Upper",
  "Pr(>|t|)"
)]

# Rename columns
names(coef_table) <- c(
  "Predictor",
  "Estimate",
  "SE",
  "95% CI Lower",
  "95% CI Upper",
  "p-value"
)

# Round numerical values
coef_table[, 2:5] <- round(coef_table[, 2:5], 3)

# Display table
knitr::kable(
  coef_table,
  caption = "Table 1. Preliminary multiple linear regression results for life satisfaction."
)
```

```{r final-diagnostic-figure, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, fig.align='center', fig.cap='Preliminary OLS diagnostics: residuals versus fitted values, normal Q-Q, scale-location, and residuals versus leverage.'}
# 4. Preliminary OLS diagnostic plots

# Arrange four diagnostic plots in a 2 x 2 layout
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

# A: Residuals vs Fitted — linearity
plot(model, which = 1)

# B: Normal Q-Q — normality
plot(model, which = 2)

# C: Scale-Location — constant variance
plot(model, which = 3)

# D: Residuals vs Leverage — influential observations
plot(model, which = 5)

# Restore default plotting layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```


```{r selected-residual-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.align='center', fig.cap='Residuals by work hours, general health, stress level, sense of belonging, and total income.'}

#5. Residual plots by selected predictors

# Create a dataset with model residuals
residual_data <- model_data
residual_data$Residuals <- residuals(model)

# 1. Residuals vs Work Hours, by Gender
p1 <- ggplot(residual_data,
             aes(x = Work_hours, y = Residuals,
                 color = Gender)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.025, width = 0.25, height = 0) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Work Hours",
    x = "Weekly Work Hours",
    y = "Residuals",
    color = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Function for categorical residual box plots
make_boxplot <- function(variable, title) {
  ggplot(residual_data,
         aes(x = .data[[variable]], y = Residuals)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "white", outlier.alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Category",
      y = "Residuals"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}

# 2. Residuals vs General Health
p2 <- make_boxplot(
  "Gen_health_state",
  "Residuals vs General Health"
)

# 3. Residuals vs Stress Level
p3 <- make_boxplot(
  "Stress_level",
  "Residuals vs Stress Level"
)

# 4. Residuals vs Sense of Belonging
p4 <- make_boxplot(
  "Sense_belonging",
  "Residuals vs Sense of Belonging"
)

# 5. Residuals vs Total Income
p5 <- make_boxplot(
  "Total_income",
  "Residuals vs Total Income"
)

# Arrange plots in a 2 x 3 layout
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
(p4 | p5 | plot_spacer())
```
